t.7.94.1: Listen, O mighty-armed Rāma, to the purpose for which I have come: I have been sent by the divine Pitāmaha, O mighty one.
t.7.94.2: O conqueror of enemy cities, in a former state of being I was your son, O hero, brought into being through māyā: I am Kāla, Time, the gatherer-in of all things.
t.7.94.3: And the Grandsire, the blessed lord, master of the worlds, has said: "O mighty-armed one, it is time for you to protect the heavenly worlds."
t.7.94.4: Long ago, having withdrawn the worlds by your own māyā, you yourself, lying upon the waters in the great ocean, first brought me forth.
t.7.94.5: Then you, having brought forth through your māyā the coiled serpent Ananta, lying upon the waters, and also two beings of mighty strength…
t.7.94.6: Madhu and Kaiṭabha as well, covered with the heaps of whose bones this earth became crowded with mountains and came to be called Medinī.
t.7.94.7: Having brought me forth in a lotus that shone like the divine sun, springing from your navel, you entrusted to me all the work of Prajāpati.
t.7.94.9: Then you too, the invincible one, from that eternal state of being, attained the nature of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings.
t.7.94.8: Thus I, having laid down my burden, have waited upon you, the lord of the world. Provide protection for all beings, for you are the one who gives me my splendour.
t.7.94.10: As the valiant son born of Aditi, increasing the joy of your brothers, you make yourself ready to help the worlds whenever tasks arise.
t.7.94.11: You, O best of the worlds, when the creatures were being terrified, desiring the slaying of Rāvaṇa, set your mind upon being among humans.
t.7.94.12: Having long ago fixed, of your own accord, the term of your own sojourn at ten thousand years and ten hundred years,
t.7.94.14: If, great king, you wish to protect and serve your subjects further, then remain, O hero, and may good fortune be yours; thus has the Grandfather spoken.
t.7.94.13: You are that mind-born son, and your full span of life among men here is complete; it is now time, O best of excellent men, for you to draw near.
t.7.94.15: Or else, O Rāghava, if you have the desire to win the world of the gods, let the gods, with Viṣṇu as their protector, be freed from their anguish.
t.7.94.17: I have heard the supremely wondrous message of the god of gods. Great indeed is the joy that has arisen in me from your coming.
t.7.94.16: Having heard the words spoken by the Grandfather and conveyed by Kāla, Rāghava, laughing, spoke words that heralded the ending of all.
t.7.94.18: May good fortune be yours; I shall go back to the very place from which I came. For you, who dwell in my heart, have been reached; of this I have no doubt.
t.7.94.19: For I must stand ready in all the undertakings of the gods, who remain obedient to my will, and at the destruction of all things, just as Pitāmaha has declared.
